docs.text: Python API Everything the logreach command does from Python code. Read lines from datetime import datetime from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo from logreach import FileEvent , Logreach reader = Logreach ( begin = datetime ( 2026 , 9 , 1 , 14 ), end = datetime ( 2026 , 9 , 1 , 15 ), timezone = ZoneInfo ( 'Europe/Vienna' )) for item in reader . read ( '/var/log' ): # a file or a directory if isinstance ( item , FileEvent ): continue # a new file starts, see below if item . timestamp is None : print ( 'no timestamp:' , item . reason , item . raw ) else : print ( item . timestamp , item . filename , item . lineno , item . raw ) read() yields, file by file, a FileEvent and then the file's lines in order, as they are read. Each line is a Logline with timestamp , raw , lineno , filename and reason . Lines without timestamp are yielded too ( timestamp is None , reason says why). They belong to the line with timestamp before them, e.g. a stack trace, and are in the time window if that line is. File events from logreach import FileEvent , FileStatus for item in reader . read ( '/var/log' ): if isinstance ( item , FileEvent ) and item . status != FileStatus . READ : print ( item . path , item . status . value , item . message ) status message READ how it is read, e.g. syslog (UTC) ; its lines follow SKIPPED why: ignored or empty UNDETERMINED no log type fits FAILED the error that stopped reading the file reader.check(path) yields only the events, e.g. to see the detected type of each file. Problems Problems never stop a run; they are collected in reader.problems : reader . problems . messages # e.g. '/var/log/app.log:3: no timestamp: ...' reader . problems . unparsed_lines # counts reader . problems . undetermined_files reader . problems . failed_files Each read() (and check() ) starts with empty problems. Options All are keyword arguments of Logreach(...) : Option Meaning begin , end datetime s of the time window; without timezone they are in timezone timezone timezone of timestamps without one (default UTC) grep , ignore_case only lines matching one of these regexes logtype 'syslog' , 'audit' , 'access' or 'json' instead of detecting the type datetime_key timestamp key, required for logtype='json' datetime_regex regex whose first group is the timestamp, for the other types dayfirst read 1/9/2026 as 1 September require_timestamp a line without timestamp stops its file ( FAILED ) fail_fast stop at the first problem types_file , ignores_file the configuration files ; default None : none are read or created ignored_extensions e.g. ['.gz'] : files in directories with these endings are skipped Invalid options raise ValueError (or TypeError for begin / end that are no datetime ). Examples Errors of the last hour, from a JSON log: from datetime import UTC , datetime , timedelta reader = Logreach ( logtype = 'json' , datetime_key = 'ts' , grep = [ 'error' ], ignore_case = True , begin = datetime . now ( UTC ) - timedelta ( hours = 1 )) errors = [ line for line in reader . read ( 'app.json' ) if not isinstance ( line , FileEvent )] Detected type of every file, with the types file of the command: for event in Logreach ( types_file = 'logtypes.json' ) . check ( '/var/log' ): print ( event . path , event . status . value , event . message ) read() is a generator: iterate over it instead of list() to keep memory low on large logs.

docs.text: Configuration Logreach reads two files from the current directory and creates them empty if they are missing. --ignore-file and --types-file choose other paths; '' turns a file off. ignore_list.txt : files to skip One regular expression per line, matched against the full path. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped. The list only applies when PATH is a directory; a file named directly is always read. # not logfiles README\Z wtmp\Z # multi-line formats apt/history\.log\Z suricata/stats\.log\Z Files with the extensions in --ignored-extensions are skipped as well (default .xz,.conf,.journal,.journal~ ; '' for none). gzip files are read, not skipped: add .gz to skip them. logtypes.json : set the type of a file JSON Lines : one object per line. A file listed here is read with this config instead of being detected. logfile_path must match the path exactly as logreach builds it from PATH . { "logfile_path" : "gather/logs/zm/web_php.log" , "type" : "syslog" , "datetimeregex" : "\\A(.+?UTC)" } { "logfile_path" : "gather/logs/nclog/audit.log" , "type" : "json" , "datetimekey" : "time" } { "logfile_path" : "gather/logs/suricata/suricata.log" , "type" : "syslog" , "dayfirst" : true } { "logfile_path" : "gather/logs/winhost/app.log" , "type" : "syslog" , "timezone" : "Europe/Vienna" } Key Required Meaning logfile_path yes path of the logfile type yes syslog , audit , access or json datetimeregex no regex whose first group is the timestamp (not for json ) datetimekey for json key that holds the timestamp dayfirst no true reads dates like 1/9/2026 as 1 September timezone no timezone of timestamps without one in this file, e.g. Europe/Vienna ; overrides --timezone --type on the command line takes precedence over this file. logreach PATH --check --interactive asks for the type of every file that is not detected and appends the answers here (see Usage ); if a path is listed twice, the last line wins.

docs.text: Contributing to Logreach Branches main : released code only development : integration branch, target for all PRs Feature branches: feature/<name> , bugfix branches: fix/<name> , created from development Workflow Open or pick an issue . For a bug, include a short sample logfile and the command that shows the problem. Branch from development . Set up the dev environment: uv sync --dev uv run --dev prek install Make your change, add tests. Run the checks: uv run --dev prek run -a uv run --dev pytest Open a PR against development and fill in the PR template. Releases See the release process .

docs.text: Release Process This document describes the steps to publish a new release of Logreach . Keeping dependencies up to date Dependency updates via Dependabot do not require a full release. If only Dependabot PRs are pending and no feature work needs to go out, merge them into main and then merge main back into development to keep both branches in sync. To merge main into development using the GitHub UI: Go to the repository on GitHub and click Pull requests , then New pull request . Set the base branch to development and the compare branch to main . Click Create pull request , add a short title (e.g. Merge main into development ), and submit. Once CI passes, merge the PR. Prerequisites Before starting a release, make sure all work intended for this version has been merged into the development branch and that CI is passing. Steps 1. Merge Dependabot PRs into main Review any open Dependabot pull requests and merge the relevant ones into main before continuing. 2. Merge development into main Open a pull request to merge the development branch into main . Once CI passes and the PR is approved, merge it. Note Merging development into main deletes the development branch. The recreate-development-branch.yml workflow recreates it from main right away. Check the Actions tab that it ran. If it failed, recreate it by hand: git checkout main git pull git checkout -b development git push -u origin development or create development from main in the GitHub UI. 3. Determine the new version number Logreach follows Semantic Versioning ( MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH ): Patch ( 0.3.x ): bug fixes, updates/correction to documentation and dependabot updates. Minor ( 0.x.0 ): new features with backwards-compatible functionality. No breaking changes. Reset the patch number to 0 . Major ( x.0.0 ): breaking changes. Reset both minor and patch numbers to 0 . 4. Bump the version number Create a new branch from main and update the version string in src/logreach/metadata.py : __date__ = 'YYYY/MM/DD' # set to the release date __version__ = '0.X.Y' # set to the new release version The version here must match the tag you will create in step 5 (e.g. version 0.4.0 corresponds to tag v0.4.0 ). Also make sure uv.lock is up to date: uv lock Commit any changes, push the branch, and open a pull request against main . Once CI passes, merge it. 5. Create a GitHub release Go to the Releases page and click Draft a new release . Set the tag to vX.Y.Z (e.g. v0.4.0 ), targeting the main branch. GitHub will create the tag on publish. Set the release title to the version string (e.g. v0.4.0 ). Click Generate release notes to populate the changelog automatically. Review the generated release notes and adjust if needed. Click Publish release . 6. Check automatically triggered workflows Publishing the release triggers the following GitHub Actions workflows automatically: Publish Docs ( publish-docs.yml ): deploys a new versioned copy of the documentation and updates the latest alias. Upload Python Package ( python-publish.yml ): checks the tag matches the package version and publishes it to PyPI . A version can be uploaded only once: a mistake needs a new version. Logreach is not published as a Docker image. Monitor the Actions tab to confirm all workflows complete successfully. Note The workflow uses PyPI trusted publishing, so no API token is stored in GitHub 7. Merge main back into development development was recreated in step 2, before the version bump landed on main . Merge main back into development so it has the new version and uv.lock , following the steps in Keeping dependencies up to date . The development branch is now ready for the next iteration of work.
docs.title: Release Process

docs.text: Usage logreach PATH [ --type ... ] [ --begin ... ] [ --end ... ] [ --check ] ... PATH is a logfile or a directory, which is walked recursively. When running from source, prefix the commands with uv run . logreach --help lists all options. Examples # all lines of one logfile, type detected automatically logreach /var/log/syslog # only the lines between two timestamps logreach /var/log/syslog --begin '2026-09-01 14:00' --end '2026-09-01 15:00' # every logfile below a directory logreach gather/logs --begin '2026-09-01 14:00' --end '2026-09-01 15:00' # only the lines in the window that match any of the regexes (--ignore-case for any case) logreach gather/logs --begin '2026-09-01 14:00' --grep 'password' --grep 'sudo:.*' # one line per log line, "timestamp path:lineno:line", e.g. to sort the lines of all files by time logreach gather/logs --begin '2026-09-01 14:00' --plain | sort # only show the detected type of each file and the problems found logreach gather/logs --check # also show on stderr why each file gets its type (which types were tried and why they failed) logreach gather/logs --check --debug # also ask for the type of each file that is not detected, and save the answers logreach gather/logs --check --interactive # do not list the problems at the end; the exit code is still 1 if there are any logreach gather/logs --quiet # stop at the first problem instead of listing all problems at the end logreach gather/logs --check --fail-fast # set the type instead of detecting it logreach audit.log --type audit logreach app.json --type json --datetime-key time logreach web_php.log --type syslog --datetime-regex '\A(.+?UTC)' # read dates like 1/9/2026 as 1 September logreach suricata.log --dayfirst How the type is chosen For each file, the first source that applies wins: --type (with --datetime-key , --datetime-regex as needed), applied to every file the file's entry in logtypes.json detection: json, audit, access and syslog are tried in this order; the first under which a line has a timestamp wins Timestamps without a year (e.g. Sep 1 13:25:26 ) take the year of --begin , else --end . Timezones Timestamps without a timezone (classic syslog like Sep 1 13:25:26 , and --begin / --end like 2026-09-01 14:00 ) are taken as UTC. Timestamps that have one, like audit epochs or 2026-09-01T14:09:21+02:00 , keep it, so files in different timezones are compared correctly. # logs and --begin / --end without timezone are Vienna time logreach gather/logs --begin '2026-09-01 14:00' --timezone Europe/Vienna A single file or host that logs in another timezone gets a "timezone" in logtypes.json , which overrides --timezone for that file. --check shows the timezone each file is read in, so a wrong assumption shows up early: gather/logs/inetfw/kern.log: syslog (UTC) gather/logs/winhost/app.log: syslog (Europe/Vienna) gather/logs/inetfw/suricata/eve.json: json (timestamp, UTC) The timezone only matters for timestamps without one; eve.json stamps like 2026-09-01T13:25:36+0000 keep their own. Checking a directory: --check --check reads every file and reports the same problems, but prints one line per file instead of the log lines: the detected type and timezone, or why the file was skipped. gather/logs/inetfw/kern.log: syslog (UTC) gather/logs/inetfw/suricata/eve.json: json (timestamp, UTC) gather/logs/inetfw/wtmp: skipped (ignored: ignore_list.txt pattern /wtmp\Z) gather/logs/inetfw/syslog.1.gz: syslog (UTC) gather/logs/inetfw/syslog.2.xz: skipped (ignored: extension .xz) gather/logs/docker/empty.log: skipped (empty) Skipped files are no problems. Without --check they are skipped without output. Teaching logreach new files: --check --interactive Run this first on a new directory. For every file whose type is not detected, --interactive ( -i ) shows its first lines and asks what to do with it: skip leaves it undetermined, so it is reported as a problem. ignore adds the file's path to ignore_list.txt . edit asks for the log type and what it needs: syslog , audit , access : Enter keeps the type's default regex; a custom regex needs a group (...) around the timestamp. json : pick the key of the timestamp from the keys of the first line. If the timestamps have no timezone, you are asked for one. Before saving, logreach shows the first parsed timestamps. If the answer reads no timestamp, or you answer n , it asks again whether to edit, ignore or skip the file. Saved answers go into logtypes.json with the path exactly as shown. To change an answer, edit or delete its line in logtypes.json ; dayfirst can be added this way if necessary. --interactive only works together with --check and in a terminal. Ctrl-D skips the remaining questions. Problems and exit codes Logreach does not stop at a problem. It lists them on stderr at the end of the run: files where no type fits lines without a timestamp, including JSON lines that are not valid JSON (e.g. cut off mid-write) errors while reading a file, e.g. a JSON line without the timestamp key --max-problems limits how many are listed, -q / --quiet lists none (the exit code still shows them), --fail-fast stops at the first one, and --require-timestamp treats a line without a timestamp as an error. Exit code Meaning 0 no problems 1 problems found 2 usage error, e.g. PATH does not exist or --type json without --datetime-key

docs.text: Run this first on a new directory. For every file whose type is not detected, --interactive ( -i ) shows its first lines and asks what to do with it: skip leaves it undetermined, so it is reported as a problem. ignore adds the file's path to ignore_list.txt . edit asks for the log type and what it needs: syslog , audit , access : Enter keeps the type's default regex; a custom regex needs a group (...) around the timestamp. json : pick the key of the timestamp from the keys of the first line. If the timestamps have no timezone, you are asked for one. Before saving, logreach shows the first parsed timestamps. If the answer reads no timestamp, or you answer n , it asks again whether to edit, ignore or skip the file. Saved answers go into logtypes.json with the path exactly as shown. To change an answer, edit or delete its line in logtypes.json ; dayfirst can be added this way if necessary. --interactive only works together with --check and in a terminal. Ctrl-D skips the remaining questions.
docs.title: Teaching logreach new files: --check --interactive

docs.text: Logreach does not stop at a problem. It lists them on stderr at the end of the run: files where no type fits lines without a timestamp, including JSON lines that are not valid JSON (e.g. cut off mid-write) errors while reading a file, e.g. a JSON line without the timestamp key --max-problems limits how many are listed, -q / --quiet lists none (the exit code still shows them), --fail-fast stops at the first one, and --require-timestamp treats a line without a timestamp as an error. Exit code Meaning 0 no problems 1 problems found 2 usage error, e.g. PATH does not exist or --type json without --datetime-key
